summary_paragraph: James, a 60-year-old man with a history of COPD, chronic alcohol dependence, and tobacco use, was readmitted one day after leaving a prior hospitalization against medical advice. He presented with shortness of breath and acute intoxication. He was treated for COPD exacerbation with prednisone, azithromycin, and bronchodilators, and his oxygen levels improved to the mid-90s on room air. His right middle lobe collapse remained unchanged on chest X-ray. He received diazepam for alcohol withdrawal and was encouraged to attend AA. Hypertension was managed with amlodipine. He was discharged home with a short-term oxycodone prescription for his right olecranon fracture pain, instructions to follow up with orthopedics and physical therapy, and a nicotine patch prescription to aid smoking cessation. He left with improved respiratory status and a plan for outpatient care.
problems: Acute alcoholic intoxication in alcoholism, unspecified
Closed fracture of olecranon process of ulna
